# X player card embed

Embeds a live, interactive page inside an X post. Same mechanism Tweetcraft and levelsio's Quake used.

## Steps
1. **Build two pages** (static site is fine):
   - Share page `/` (the link pasted into the post) with absolute https meta tags:
     - `twitter:card=player`
     - `twitter:player=https://<domain>/play`
     - `twitter:player:width=480`, `twitter:player:height=480`
     - `twitter:image=https://<domain>/preview.png` (fallback still; shown on mobile and before load)
     - `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:site`, plus matching `og:` tags
     - Human visitors to `/` should also see the experience (e.g. iframe `/play` full width).
   - `/play`: self-contained 480x480 responsive page doing the live part. Fetch fresh data (e.g. `/data.json?t=<now>`) and re-poll so content updates without reposting.
2. **Headers** so X can frame it:
   - `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' https://x.com https://*.x.com https://twitter.com https://*.twitter.com`
   - Never send `X-Frame-Options`.
   - `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/play` and data files; short cache on images.
3. **Host** over HTTPS with no mixed content. Vercel (headers in `vercel.json`) or Cloudflare Pages (`_headers` file). Log in a CLI with its device-code flow (e.g. `npx vercel login`), send the user the device link, never ask for tokens. A free `<name>.vercel.app` alias can be set with `vercel alias set`, then redeploy `--prod` so it serves.
4. **Verify** with curl: `/` returns the tags with absolute URLs, `/play` and data return 200 with the CSP and no X-Frame-Options. Test `/play` in headless Chrome at desktop and iPhone emulation (DPR 3).
5. **Post**: paste only the link, no attached image (an image replaces the card). Use a fresh post, not a quote post. Check on desktop that it plays inline.

## Gotchas
- X caches card metadata (title, description, image) about 7 days. The iframe content is live, so update data, not tags. Add `?v=2` to force a fresh card.
- Inline play is desktop web. Mobile apps show the image and open the page in a browser, so make `/play` mobile friendly: `touch-action: none` only on interactive areas, pointer events, 16px inputs to avoid iOS zoom.
- On iOS Safari, scaling a tiny element with CSS transform looks blurry. Render enlarged items at their real pixel size with high-res sources.
- X's policy may limit player cards to audio and video and it has paused them before. Treat it as experimental and keep a good fallback image.
- Avoid engagement-bait wording ("reply to get in") in the post, card text, and page; X may hide the post. Put instructions in a self-reply instead.

# Getting started
I turn your site or idea into an X player card: a live page that plays inside your X post.

Ask one at a time, adapting to answers:
1. What site or idea do you want inside your post? Ask for the URL if one exists. If they share an existing site, ask whether to embed it as-is or build a dedicated 480x480 /play view.
2. Where should it be hosted: Vercel or Cloudflare Pages, and do they already have an account or domain? If none, suggest a free vercel.app subdomain.
3. What X handle should go in twitter:site?

Then: save their answers as memories and start the X player card embed skill right away. For CLI login, use the device-code flow and send them the link; never ask for tokens. Mention up front that X has paused player cards before, so a fallback image is always included.
